conbody.p: Impact, under Verify in the project menu, answers "what does a change to this requirement touch?" before you make it. Pick the requirement, or open the page from Show impact → on a requirement or a row of the Traceability Matrix. The analysis starts from a requirement and flows from it to every artifact its links lead to.

ul.li: Picking the requirement. The list on the left holds the project's requirements as the requirements page's Table does, under the headings they sit in, each with its reference and title; fold a heading with its caret. Type in the search bar above it to narrow the list: a reference such as REQ-73, part of a title, or a chip from its caret (status, priority, owner, dates, Mine, In review). Click a requirement to run its impact; it stays highlighted. ‹ Hide list folds the list away to give the result the width, and › Show list brings it back. On a phone the list sits above the result and folds away once you pick.

The result is a tree diagram with the requirement in the middle. Upstream — what it depends on, its sources and rationale — branches out to the left; Downstream — what depends on it, what a change here could affect — branches out to the right. Each artifact hangs off the one it was reached through.

Each connector is coloured and labelled by its link type, with a link key below the tree, so a satisfies reads apart from a verifies or a mitigates at a glance. Colour by colours the boxes by their type or their review status, with a colour key beside it.
Select a box to open the artifact. ⌖ on a box re-centres the impact on that artifact, so you can follow a design item or a test case on from there.

− and + beside a box fold and unfold what hangs off it, and the number beside a folded box says how many artifacts it hides. Drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, and Fit shows the whole tree. With the keyboard, the arrow keys walk the tree and fold its branches, and Enter opens the artifact.

Depth — 1 shows only the artifacts linked directly to the requirement, 2 and 3 stop that many links away, and All follows every link to the end of the chain. Only the depths the result reaches are offered.

Table shows the same result as a table, one row per artifact: its direction, how many links away it is, the link it came through and the artifact it was reached through, its reference, title, type and status, and Centre to re-centre on it. It reads well with a screen reader and copies out cleanly. Tree goes back to the diagram.

The walk follows every link, hop after hop. Downstream it reaches the sub-requirements, the design items that satisfy them, the test cases that verify them and the hazards those design items mitigate; upstream it reaches the user needs and parent requirements. An impacts link counts as the change flowing from its source to its target, and a relates-to link, having no direction, is followed both ways.

conbody.p: Run it before changing an approved requirement: the downstream list is the set of artifacts whose links will turn suspect and that may need review again.
